newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bavarian banks deny getting tax help for merger.
newsitem.headline: Bavarian banks deny getting tax help for merger.

text.p: Two Bavarian banks which plan to merge to form a new German banking giant said on Thursday they were sure shareholders would accept the share swap crucial to the deal and denied they got preferential tax treatment.

Bayerische Vereinsbank AG and Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG (Hypo-Bank) said the tax efficient way in which the merger will be conducted is possible everywhere in Germany, and has also been used outside Bavaria.
Under the deal, which will create Germany's Number Two bank, Vereinsbank is offering to exchange most of its 10 percent stake in insurer Allianz AG for a stake of up to 45 percent in Hypo-Bank.

Analysts say the swap, which under a 1958 tax ruling exempts Vereinsbank from paying tax on the realisation of billions of marks of reserves locked in its Allianz stake, could set a precedent for similar merger deals in the sector.

The offer of one Allianz share for six Hypo-Bank shares runs from August 4 to September 10 and paves the way for a fusion, terms for which will be based on the banks' 1997 accounts. The merger will be prepared from October.

"We're convinced that the offer is right, that the strategy is right, and that we'll manage to get 40 percent," Hypo-Bank management board member Martin Koelsch told a news conference at which the banks detailed terms of the merger.
The merger would fall through if Vereinsbank got less than 40 percent because it would not attain a sufficient majority of voting rights to approve the deal.
Executives said institutional investors had shown a lot of interest in the share exchange.

The merger plan has been praised as an elegant way to allow banks to dispose of their huge shareholdings across finance and industry and unlock hidden reserves without having to pay a crippling 60 percent capital gains tax.

But rival bankers have suggested the tax ruling, known as the Tauschgutachten, was applied more leniently in Munich than would be the case in Frankfurt, home to Germany's top three banks Deutsche Bank AG, Dresdner Bank AG and Commerzank AG.
Analysts have argued that Munich authorities aided the merger to fend off a possible takeover of Vereinsbank or Hypo-Bank and to put Munich on the map as a financial centre to rival Frankfurt.
Vereinsbank management board member Stephan Schueller dismissed the suggestion as "nonsense."
"The Tauschgutachten is also applied in other states including Hesse (where Frankfurt is located), in the chemical sector. It's not at all peculiar to Bavaria."
The Tauschgutachten allows companies to avoid tax by swapping assets, albeit only in cases where the assets to be swapped are of equal type and value.

Banking sources said the method was used by Frankfurt-based chemicals group Hoechst AG which in December announced plans to merge some of its specialty chemicals businesses with Swiss group Clariant AG.

Executives at both banks said Hypo-Bank shareholders should accept the exchange offer which would allow them take profits from the share price gain of more than 30 percent since the merger plan was announced on July 21.

Hypo-Bank's shares closed down 1.07 marks at 76.53 marks on Thursday, up 30.8 percent from its level of 58.50 marks on July 18. Allianz closed at 470 marks, down 9.50 marks on the day. The shares now roughly match the six for one ratio.
The banks plan to woo Hypo-Bank's 90,000 small shareholders with television and newspaper advertisements and have set up a telephone hotline.

The campaign started on Thursday with executives singing the praises of Allianz shares and warning that Hypo-Bank's shares were likely to fall back to their pre-July 21 level once the exchange offer was over.

Hypo-Bank management board member Martin Koelsch said Allianz shares had potential to keep rising given that its portfolio of disclosed shareholdings at present accounted for only about 55 percent of its market capitalisation.
Koelsch added: "The market for Hypo-Bank shares will become very tight after the exchange, so it will be hard to sell them later."
The exchange is being carried out by Vereinsbank's Hamburg-based unit Vereins- und West-Bank AG.

Vereinsbank said it would use up to 19.3 million Allianz shares from its portfolio -- equivalent to a stake of up to 8.4 percent in Allianz -- to acquire the Hypo-Bank stake. --Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525
